messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Redacted]
Date of Birth: [Redacted]
Gender: Female
Admission Date: [Redacted]
Discharge Date: [Redacted]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted following diagnosis of mucosal malignant melanoma of the hard palate. The tumor was found to have extensively spread within the hard palate with no involvement of the nasal cavity or nasopharynx, and with no neck lymph node metastasis.

Treatment:
The patient refused surgery and underwent CIR at another facility as the initial treatment, followed by concurrent chemotherapy. After one cycle of chemotherapy was stopped due to severe hematological toxicity. The patient achieved a complete response following CIR and was monitored by physical examinations, endoscopy, enhanced CT, and MRI. At 16 months after CIR, a cervical metastasis of a left jugular lymph node was detected, leading to diagnosis of stage crT0N1M0 MMMHN. The patient was treated by en bloc salvage ND with preservation of the accessory nerve, internal jugular vein, and sternocleidomastoid muscle. The duration of surgery was 132 min, and blood loss was less than 10 mL. The patient was discharged on postoperative Day 7.

Postoperative Management:
The patient experienced no Clavien-Dindo grade 3 or 4 postoperative complications. No recurrence was found by the whole-body enhanced CT performed 3 months after surgery.
Final Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-up Care:
Patient will continue to be monitored for any signs of recurrence or metastasis.

Discussions:
The patient was presented with several treatment options, including radiotherapy and systemic immunotherapy, before choosing surgery. The en bloc salvage ND with preservation of the accessory nerve, internal jugular vein, and sternocleidomastoid muscle was performed successfully, and the patient experienced no postoperative complications.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
This admission was for salvage neck dissection of a cervical lymph node metastasis from a mucosal malignant melanoma of the hard palate. The primary tumor had a complete response to carbon-ion radiotherapy (CIR) and shows no recurrence, so the stage is crT0.

There are two candidate categories:
- **C79** (secondary malignant neoplasm of other sites, which includes lymph node metastasis) fits if the metastasis is coded as the reason for admission. Lymph node secondaries would normally go to C77.
- **C06** (malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of mouth, which includes the palate) fits if the melanoma is coded as the primary site. Melanoma of the mouth is not coded to C43, because C43 covers skin melanoma only.

For a lymph node metastasis, the coding would be C77 (secondary and unspecified malignant neoplasm of lymph nodes). The neck node is the condition treated, and the primary is in remission after treatment. Under the usual convention, the principal diagnosis is the metastatic site being treated, which is the lymph node, so C77.

**C77**
